name: LIBERO: Benchmarking Knowledge Transfer for Lifelong Robot Learning
description: LIBERO (Lifelong Benchmark for Robot Learning) is a standardized benchmark and human demonstration dataset designed to evaluate lifelong robot learning and knowledge transfer. Developed by UT Austin and Sony AI, LIBERO encompasses 130 manipulation tasks across four distinct task suites implemented in robosuite: LIBERO-Spatial (10 tasks testing spatial variations), LIBERO-Object (10 tasks testing novel object instances), LIBERO-Goal (10 tasks testing distinct goals in fixed scenes), and LIBERO-100 (a long-horizon suite partitioned into LIBERO-10 and LIBERO-90). The dataset contains 6,500 high-quality human teleoperated demonstrations (exactly 50 demonstrations per task) with synchronized multi-camera RGB video, robot proprioception, and language instructions.
